sections.title: Information collected
sections.body: We collect the information needed for your care: identification, contact details, medical and dental information relevant to the safety and quality of care.

sections.title: Use of information
sections.body: Your information is used to organize appointments, maintain the clinical record, deliver care, follow up and communicate as needed for your care.

sections.title: Sharing of information
sections.body: Your information is only shared when necessary for care, for a referral to another professional, for collaboration with the laboratory, or when required by law.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Reasonable technical and organizational measures are in place to protect your information against loss, unauthorized access, modification or unintended disclosure.

sections.title: Access and correction
sections.body: You may request access to your information or correction of inaccurate details. An identity check may be required before processing the request.

sections.title: Consent
sections.body: Your consent is required to transmit certain information or documents (specialist referral, transmission to the laboratory, electronic communications). You may withdraw your consent for purposes not essential to care.

sections.title: Electronic communication
sections.body: Communications by email, SMS or web form may involve risks inherent to digital transit. The information transmitted should be limited to what is necessary for the request. For particularly sensitive information, an in-person or phone exchange may be preferable.

sections.title: Person responsible for the protection of personal information
sections.body: For any question regarding privacy, access to or correction of your personal information, or data security, you may contact the [de facto] Dental Studio's person responsible for the protection of personal information by phone or email. [de facto] Dental Studio operates under the laws applicable in Quebec and Canada, in particular the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (Law 25) and PIPEDA at the federal level.

blocs.texte: Dr Bader Ramdani, general dentist, born in Montreal. A 2021 doctor of dental medicine from Université Laval in Quebec City, he is a member of the Ordre des dentistes du Québec. He founded Studio [de facto] in Ahuntsic, with a denture workshop on site, to give himself the time to examine, to explain and to treat. He sees patients in French and in English.
The studio team welcomes you, calls you back to confirm your appointments, helps you with your insurance and stays with you from one visit to the next.
Every complete examination ends with a written oral health report that you keep. It is the starting point for your decisions and your follow-up.
The studio gives free oral health workshops with neighbourhood community organizations.

parcours.metaTitre: The [de facto] path — understanding before treating
parcours.metaDescription: A path in five stages, from the complete examination to follow-up. A stage is a family of care objectives, not a level of severity.
parcours.titre: The [de facto] path: understanding before treating
parcours.intro: A well-informed patient is worth two. Our goal is not that you accept a treatment, but that you understand your mouth. Well informed, you decide better, and for yourself.

schema.intro: A [de facto] stage is a family of care objectives, not a level of severity. No one has to go through them all: you define your care objectives.

stades.nom: Restore the function of the teeth
stades.texte: Repair locally, within the current framework of your mouth.
Change global parameters: occlusion, vertical dimension, alignment.

detail.texte: The complete examination and, if needed, further examinations. We establish the starting picture.
We first control infection and inflammation: active decay, diseased gums, infected teeth.

detail.titre: Restore the function of the teeth
detail.texte: Repair locally, within the current framework of your mouth.
Prevention and follow-up. This stage begins at the very first appointment and never ends.
A transformation that requires changing global parameters in the mouth: occlusion, vertical dimension of occlusion, alignment of the teeth, and so on.

parcours.note: Stage 4 is neither mandatory nor superior to stage 2. An emergency is treated separately, at any time.
parcours.savoirTitre: What you will know at the end of the examination

savoir.texte: what is going well, and what is not.
what is urgent, what can wait, what is optional.
the prognoses, the benefits, the limits and their costs.
advice on hygiene and prevention, whether or not you go ahead with treatment.

parcours.savoirNote: The plan is explained to you at the desk, never in the dental chair. You receive a written summary of your condition.

change.texte: Shade, shape and smile checked directly in the mouth. When a tooth's colour is hard to match, she comes and looks at it in the studio's own light rather than working from a photograph.

change.titre: The making is done from start to finish here.
change.texte: Except the metal framework of partial dentures. An adjustment is often made while you wait, instead of a second appointment a week later.

change.titre: One person makes it. One person supervises.
change.texte: She makes your piece from beginning to end. Dr Ramdani supervises every step. If there is a question about your case, it is settled between two pieces, not by email between two businesses.

atelier.equipementNote: Externally: digitizing of conventional impressions and metal frameworks.
atelier.equipeTexte: The workshop is made up of Dr Ramdani, general dentist and founder of studio [de facto], and a dental technologist, Amira Thameur, who graduated in 2022 and is a member of the Ordre des technologues en prothèses et appareils dentaires du Québec. Dr Ramdani plans and supervises every piece; Amira Thameur makes it and finishes it by hand. Hand finishing is what separates a correct piece from one you never notice: it is the last tenth of a millimetre, and no machine does it for you.

questions.q: How long does the first appointment take?
questions.r: A focused consultation takes 30 minutes, a complete examination about an hour, and a complete examination with cleaning about an hour and a half. For a complex case, a second appointment at the consultation desk is used to go over the treatment plan.

questions.q: Are you open evenings or weekends?
questions.r: For now, Wednesday until 8 p.m.; the studio is closed Thursday through Sunday. Dr Ramdani plans to open the studio full time: new hours are coming.

questions.q: How do I cancel or move an appointment?
questions.r: Call 514 863-7805 at least 24 hours ahead, ideally 48. Fees apply from the second appointment missed without notice.

questions.q: Do you accept the Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)?
questions.r: Yes. Bring your card to the first visit.
For children under 10 and recipients of a financial assistance program with a claim booklet, several services are covered.

questions.q: Do you accept my private insurance?
What methods of payment do you accept?
Will I know the price before a treatment?
questions.r: Yes. You receive a written estimate before we begin, and you decide.

questions.q: I am afraid of the dentist. What do you do?
questions.r: We explain every step before doing it, and you can ask for a break at any time. Tell us when you book.

questions.q: Will I be obliged to have treatment after the examination?
questions.r: No. You receive the information and the options, including what happens if nothing is done.
